prerequisites: the notions of three-dimensional kinematics and dynamics of the rigid body as seen in the LEPL1202 course as well as the kinematic principles of the basic mechanisms seen in the LMECA1210 course
mastery of the following numerical methods: Newton-Raphson method, interpolation methods and numerical integration scheme as seen in the LEPL1104 course
a sufficient mastery of the basic principles of the C language (language elements, programming, structures, pointers, compilation/execution), as seen in the LEPL1104 course or the LEPL1503 project

learning_outcomes.text: analyze an existing system and improve it
distinguish between reality and the models used to describe or modify it
understand the notion of uncertainty in the management of the project, in its realization, and in the results obtained
develop a computer application allowing the simulation of complex multi-body systems in small groups of students

apply in a multidisciplinary way the skills acquired in mechanics (for example, in the fields of solid mechanics, dynamic systems, methods, etc.) and numerical methods (integration, resolution of nonlinear equations, etc.)
acquire and use new knowledge and advanced techniques related to the application (consultation of scientific literature and reference books, contacts with experts, etc.)
implement and test a technical solution and compare it with real data

syllabus_topics: Bibliographic research and drafting of specifications
Development of the appropriate methodology to solve a problem
Development of algorithms and programming (PYTHON, ROBOTRAN, etc.)
Analysis of simulations and evaluation of the performance of the system studied
Possibly, simple experiments to validate or feed the model and simulations
teaching_methods: Work in small groups under the supervision of a tutor
Audience sessions for the introduction or restructuring of specific concepts useful for the realization of the project
Intermediate presentations of the progress of the project

assessment_methods.method: continuous assessment (intermediate reports and presentations, written report, final presentation)

assessment_rules: The weighting for continuous assessment is 3/4 if the individual written exam mark is higher than 10/20. The weighting is 0 if the individual written exam mark is less than 6/20. The weighting is linearly progressive between 0 for an individual written exam score of 6/20 and 3/4 for a score of 10/20. The continuous assessment mark acquired in the first term is retained in the event of a second term and cannot be repeated.
degree: Bachelor in Engineering (Bachelier en sciences de l'ingénieur, orientation ingénieur civil) - FSA1BA
